text: Python components are discovered from their syntax, never by running them (#304, #307). Discovery parses each non-test source file in an explicit Python scope with the standard library's ast, through python3 -I -S on the host or in the plumbing sandbox, with the source on stdin, so no project code, decorator or default runs. Every function and method, synchronous or asynchronous, decorated or nested, is a component identified as python:<dotted module>#<symbol>@<path>. Nested ones are named like qualname, and repeated names get ordinals in source order. A component's contract hash covers the exact bytes of its direct Requires, Ensures, Exsures and Decreases calls, apart from its body and comments, and its source hash covers the whole file. Go discovery is unchanged, TypeScript discovery stays refused, and explicit component checks stay refused until adapters run them.
